problem_statement: The overseer subsystem has accreted complexity across many issue-driven patches. The auto-file-issue path is starved upstream because many failure modes never produce a Tier-1 alert. The overseer lifecycle has asymmetries with phase agents, signal coverage has systematic gaps across orchestrator runtime, worktree/branch, container/K8s, gateway, BRC, HITL, cost, self-health, external state, and LLM substrate layers. Dead code (issue_filer.py) persists. The 2,024-line monitor.py is bolted-on rather than composed.

refine_decisions_consumed.cq-1: Soft cap with repetition detector — escalate if recent logs are >N% repetitive content
refine_decisions_consumed.cq-2: Per-pipeline inference — aggregate failures over sliding window for LLM substrate

refine_decisions_consumed.feedback-1_Q1: Generation token primitive must be defined and implemented as prerequisite. Recommended: orchestrator pod UID (K8s) or UUID minted at startup, surfaced on health-status response.

AD-1_tier1_for_new_checks.decision: All new signal-coverage checks go into orchestrator/health_checks/tier1/ as new files implementing the HealthCheck protocol (types.py:88).
AD-1_tier1_for_new_checks.rationale: monitor.py is 2,024 lines and scheduled for #2261 slice-7 decomposition. Adding checks to monitor.py would conflict with that slice and violate the 1,500-line cap. New tier1 checks compose with the existing runner (runner.py:42 register()) and EventBus, keeping them independently testable and avoiding monitor.py bloat.
AD-1_tier1_for_new_checks.constraint: Each new check file self-registers via HealthCheckRunner.register() at orchestrator startup. Concurrent slices add registration lines to a common startup file — minor merge-conflict, trivially resolved.

AD-2_no_monitor_decomposition.decision: This issue does NOT extract or restructure monitor.py internals.
AD-2_no_monitor_decomposition.rationale: monitor.py decomposition is owned by #2261 slice-7 (scheduled, in-flight). This issue's cleanup scope is: delete dead code (issue_filer.py), remove dead action paths, consolidate lifecycle seams in pipelines.py.

AD-3_overseer_phase_peer.decision: Overseer lifecycle is a phase peer: spawn WITH phase agents, tear down WITH phase agents, no overseer alone between phases.
AD-3_overseer_phase_peer.rationale: The issue explicitly states this as Goal 1. Currently overseer spawns BEFORE agents (pipelines.py:21888) and has a dedicated respawn loop (lines 520-683). The asymmetry must be resolved.
AD-3_overseer_phase_peer.implementation_approach: Move spawn into the phase-agent spawn loop. If agents fail to spawn, overseer spawn is skipped. Consolidate 5 teardown call sites into one pre_event_hook factory (the _make_overseer_teardown_hook at line 20864 is already a step in this direction).

AD-4_respawn_convergence.decision: Resolve the respawn asymmetry: either fold overseer respawn into agent restart machinery, or document why it needs its own path.
AD-4_respawn_convergence.approach: After analysis, the overseer respawn loop serves a distinct purpose (infrastructure liveness vs agent behavioral restart). Rather than merging the paths, document the asymmetry as intentional and align the mechanics: overseer respawn respects the same run_epoch guard (#1916), respects the same overseer_lock, and clears overseer-local state on respawn (analogous to restart_phase clearing state).
AD-4_respawn_convergence.rationale: Overseer respawn handles infrastructure failures (container EXITED/FAILED/NOT_FOUND) while agent restart handles behavioral issues (stall, misalignment). Keeping them separate preserves the distinct semantics but the state-clearing gap must be closed.

AD-5_restart_state_clearing.decision: restart_agent for a specific agent must clear that agent's tracking state in OverseerMonitor: _escalation_history[agent_role], _agents_restart_exhausted (remove role), per-agent stall counters.
AD-5_restart_state_clearing.rationale: Current behavior: restarted agent inherits stale counters from the dead process. Next stall counted as 'attempt #N+1' of an N-deep history that belongs to a dead process.
AD-5_restart_state_clearing.implementation: The REST restart-agent endpoint (or the overseer's _execute_restart_agent at monitor.py:700) must emit a state-clearing event. OverseerMonitor listens for restart events and calls a new _clear_agent_state(agent_role) method.

AD-6_generation_token.decision: Add a generation token to orchestrator health-status responses. Value: K8s pod UID when on K8s, or a UUID minted at orchestrator startup.
AD-6_generation_token.rationale: Refine feedback-1 Q1 confirmed this primitive does not exist. It is a prerequisite for recycle-detection (orchestrator pod restarts mid-phase while agent/overseer survive, leaving in-memory counters aligned with old generation).
AD-6_generation_token.scope: Production primitive — the orchestrator's health-status route returns the generation token. The overseer reads it on each poll cycle; on mismatch, resets state and emits orchestrator_generation_change alert.

AD-7_repetition_detector.decision: Implement a log-content repetition detector as part of the incomplete-consensus stall check, not as a standalone module.
AD-7_repetition_detector.rationale: cq-1 resolved 'soft cap with repetition detector'. The incomplete_consensus_stall tier1 check (328 lines) already has activity-aware suppression (#1609). Extending it with a repetition-aware activity test is the natural home. When recent container logs are >N% repetitive content AND the stall exceeds a soft cap, treat agent activity as non-progress and escalate regardless.

AD-8_llm_substrate_per_pipeline.decision: LLM substrate health uses per-pipeline inference via a sliding failure window per pipeline, not cluster-wide signals.
AD-8_llm_substrate_per_pipeline.rationale: cq-2 resolved 'per-pipeline inference'. The overseer already tracks LLM call failures via OverseerSelfMonitor.record_llm_call(). Extend this to track failure windows: if >N% of classification/advisor calls fail in a T-second window, emit overseer_classifier_unhealthy / overseer_advisor_unhealthy alerts.

AD-9_template_per_check.decision: Each new tier1 check that emits alerts also adds its template entry to shared/egg_overseer/issue_template.py.
AD-9_template_per_check.rationale: Keeps each check self-contained. Template entries are small (dict additions). Avoids a template-only slice that would need to know all alert types in advance.

AD-10_slice_dag_affinity.decision: Health checks running in slice-DAG implement phase need EGG_SLICE_ID affinity. Alerts carry the slice ID of the slice they monitor.
AD-10_slice_dag_affinity.rationale: In slice-DAG implement, N slices run concurrently but there is one phase-scoped overseer. Per-slice dedup/escalation windows must not collide. The health check context (context.py) already has pipeline_id and phase; add optional slice_id propagation.

slice_composition.forest_validation: Every slice has ≤1 DAG parent. No multi-parent violations.
slice_composition.rationale: Slice 1 is the foundation cleanup (dead code + lifecycle ordering). Slices 2-7 extend independently from it in parallel. Slice 8 (self-health/LLM substrate) depends on slice 2 (generation token). Slice 9 (filing infrastructure) depends on slice 8 (last signal slice). Signal slices are grouped by layer affinity: orchestrator runtime (3), worktree/gateway (4), BRC/consensus (5), container/K8s/HITL/cost (6), external state (7) — each is one coherent BRC cycle of work.

risks_identified.risk: Concurrent tier1 check slices modifying tier1/__init__.py simultaneously
risks_identified.mitigation: Each check registers via HealthCheckRunner.register() at startup. __init__.py re-exports are batched per slice or handled via a registration discovery mechanism to minimize merge conflicts.

risks_identified.risk: monitor.py changes across multiple slices (dead code removal in slice-1, state clearing in slice-2, self-monitor wiring in slice-8)
risks_identified.mitigation: Slice-1 changes are deletions (low conflict risk). Slice-2 adds new methods (additive). Slice-8 wires existing methods into new call sites (additive). Stacked-PR serialization handles remaining conflicts.

risks_identified.risk: pipelines.py is 24,578 lines — lifecycle changes in slices 1-2 are in the same file
risks_identified.mitigation: Slice-1 changes (spawn ordering, teardown consolidation) and slice-2 changes (respawn alignment, generation token) affect different regions of the file. Slice-2 depends on slice-1 so they don't run concurrently.

risks_identified.risk: Generation token primitive (AD-6) requires changes to orchestrator route handler — may need gateway policy consideration
risks_identified.mitigation: The generation token is read-only metadata on the health-status response. No gateway mutation. Minimal attack surface.

risks_identified.risk: Repetition detector (AD-7, cq-1) requires log-content analysis which may be expensive for high-volume agents
risks_identified.mitigation: Sample recent N log lines (configurable), compute entropy or n-gram repetition ratio in O(N*window). Only invoked when incomplete-consensus stall is already detected. Not on every poll cycle.

risks_identified.risk: Slice-DAG affinity (AD-10) requires slice_id propagation through health check context
risks_identified.mitigation: Extend PipelineHealthContext with optional slice_id. Checks that don't need slice affinity ignore it. Backward compatible.

risks_identified.risk: #2261 slice-7 (monitor.py decomposition) landing during this issue's implementation
risks_identified.mitigation: This issue avoids restructuring monitor.py. If slice-7 lands first, our monitor.py changes (dead code removal, method additions) apply to the decomposed modules. If ours lands first, slice-7 decomposes with our changes included.

out_of_scope_references: #2272 — overseer internal architecture (Sonnet executor + specialist subagents). Parallel track.
